    Cumulative meta-analysis

    Source: R/meta-sensitivity.R
    meta_cumulative.Rd

    meta_cumulative() adds studies one at a time, in the order given by order (for example publication year), and reports the pooled estimate after each addition.

    Usage

    meta_cumulative(
  .data,
  order = NULL,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  method = "REML",
  test = "z",
  level = 0.95,
  decreasing = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A <meta_fit> from meta_pool() (its estimator and test are reused), a <meta_es> or a data frame.

    order

    <data-masking> A variable that defines the order in which studies are added. Evaluated in the data used to fit the model. Defaults to the row order.

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    method, test

    Used only when .data is not a <meta_fit>.

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    decreasing

    Add studies in decreasing order of order?

    Value

    A tibble with one row per step: the study added, the number of studies so far (k), estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, tau2 and I2.

    References

    Lau, J., Antman, E. M., Jimenez-Silva, J., Kupelnick, B., Mosteller, F. and Chalmers, T. C. (1992). Cumulative meta-analysis of therapeutic trials for myocardial infarction. New England Journal of Medicine, 327(4), 248-254. doi:10.1056/NEJM199207233270406

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg,
  study = author
)
meta_pool(bcg) |> meta_cumulative(order = year)
